topPRs.title: kona-sp1: Reuse derivation pipelines across super-range claims
topPRs.author: Inphi
topPRs.body:
Super-range execution currently rebuilds the derivation pipeline for every claimed L2 block, repeating L1 traversal, channel reconstruction, decompression, and batch decoding.

This change groups chain-local transitions with contiguous output roots and reuses one pipeline and driver per segment. Each progressing claim advances the same driver and retains output-root and exact block-number validation. No-op transitions preserve continuity without advancing the driver; a changed agreed root after consolidation starts a fresh segment.

Public inputs, encodings, commitments, and timestamp-major output ordering remain unchanged.

## Why

Channel reconstruction is a major cost of super-range guest execution. In a pre-change four-block OP Mainnet [canary](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22791), it consumed **8.085 billion cycles—87% of payload derivation**. Each block repeated 147 lower-pipeline pulls, covering L1 traversal, frame/channel assembly, decompression, and batch decoding.

A prototype using the same pipeline-reuse approach demonstrated the intended behavior: all 147 channel pulls occurred during the first block, with **zero channel-reconstruction calls for the remaining three blocks**.

| Measurement | Before | Reuse prototype |
|---|---:|---:|
| Channel-reconstruction calls | 588 | 147 |
| Channel-reconstruction cycles | 8.085B | 2.059B |
| Payload-derivation cycles | 9.296B | 2.397B |
| Range PGU | 17.926B | 6.073B |

The results are similar on a 24-block span - the remaining 23 block derivations reuse the result of the channel reconstructed from the first block derivation. Granting us further cycle count reduction in the super-range program.

fixes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/22747

topPRs.title: op-chain-ops: Support interop kona prestates in check-prestate
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
`check-prestate` could not review a `cannon64-kona-interop` prestate, and could not resolve the superchain-registry pin for recent kona-client tags.

Two fixes:

- `gitlinkCommit` resolved the submodule path relative to the working directory. Run from the `op-chain-ops/cmd/check-prestate` directory the README documents, the lookup found nothing and the tool reported the pin as missing. The legacy `superchain-registry-commit.txt` lookup is root-relative, so this only surfaced once tags moved to the submodule gitlink. Fixed with `--full-tree`, covered by a regression test that fails on the current code.
- The prestate type check rejected `cannon64-kona-interop`. Both kona variants are built from the same kona-client tag, so they share a registry pin and chain configs; only the build features differ.

Found while reviewing the kona-client v1.7.0-rc.2 prestates.

topPRs.title: ci: improve Kontrol execution
topPRs.author: mds1
topPRs.body:
Moves Kontrol execution from RV-hosted compute to our CircleCI runners after each merge to develop.

- Updates Kontrol to 1.0.255, preserving symbolic caller coverage.
- Reports proof failures directly in CI and improves Slack failure notifications.
- Retains proof artifacts and JUnit results, including diagnostics on failure.
- Keeps the existing xlarge runner, disables Docker layer caching, and avoids uploading duplicate proof archives to reduce costs.

All 16 proofs pass locally and in CircleCI. The existing 32 GiB runner completed in 25m55s with 25.1 GiB sampled peak memory, using about 37% fewer compute credits than the 64 GiB benchmark. All CI checks pass. No contract behavior changes. Live Slack delivery has not been tested.

- [ ] After merge, confirm no other consumers use the RV CircleCI context or dispatch credential, then retire them.
